title: Rishabh Pant Has Given Up the LSG Captaincy. He Wanted to Quit Mid-Season.
excerpt: The most expensive player in IPL history finished last with Lucknow for the second straight year. Reports say he told the franchise he was done weeks before the season ended.
body:
Rishabh Pant is no longer the captain of the Lucknow Super Giants. The franchise confirmed on Friday that the 28-year-old wicketkeeper-batter had requested to be relieved of his leadership duties, and the management had accepted with immediate effect.

What the official statement did not say is that Pant wanted out weeks earlier. According to India Today, the left-hander had told the franchise he wanted to step down during the middle of IPL 2026, while the team was still playing. He was asked to reconsider. He did not change his mind. With each loss, the resolve only hardened.

## Two Seasons, No Playoffs, One Record Price Tag

Pant joined LSG ahead of IPL 2025 for a tournament-record ₹27 crore at the mega auction in Jeddah. He was the most expensive player in IPL history, and owner Sanjiv Goenka declared that his captaincy would one day be spoken about in the same breath as MS Dhoni and Rohit Sharma.

Two seasons later, the comparison sounds like a different sport. LSG finished seventh in 2025 and tenth — dead last — in 2026, winning just four of 14 matches. Across both campaigns under Pant, the franchise never came close to the playoffs.

Pant's own numbers tell the story. In IPL 2026, he scored 312 runs from 13 innings at an average of 28.36 and a strike rate of 138.05 with a single half-century. There were moments — a 68 against Sunrisers Hyderabad, a cameo of 32 off 10 balls against RCB — but they were islands in a sea of frustration.

## The Bigger Picture Is Bleaker

The captaincy exit is not an isolated event. Pant's standing in Indian cricket has been slipping for months.

Before the IPL ended, the BCCI stripped him of the Test vice-captaincy, handing the role to KL Rahul ahead of the one-off Test against Afghanistan on June 6. He has also been dropped from the ODI squad. For a player who once seemed destined to lead India across formats, the trajectory has reversed sharply.

The franchise is now looking at Aiden Markram and Mitchell Marsh as potential replacements for the captaincy. Tom Moody, LSG's Director of Cricket, said the focus was now on "rebuilding and restructuring to reach the best standards."

## What Went Wrong

Reports paint a picture of a dressing room with too many voices and too little clarity. Moody's role as Director of Cricket meant that on-field decisions were not always Pant's alone. The squad, built around Pant, Nicholas Pooran, and Mitchell Marsh, lacked bowling depth and tactical balance.

Pant was visibly frustrated through much of the season. For a player who thrives on instinct and aggression, the environment at LSG appears to have been suffocating. The ₹27 crore price tag — a number that was supposed to validate his standing — became a weight that followed him into every press conference and every failure.

## What NRI Fans Should Know

Pant remains contracted to LSG. He has not been released or traded. But the captaincy exit, combined with the international demotions, means he enters the next phase of his career needing to prove himself as a player, not a leader.

The one-off Test against Afghanistan at the Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru on June 6 will be his next opportunity in international cricket. It is the kind of match — a one-off game against a lower-ranked side — that should be low-pressure. For Pant, nothing feels low-pressure right now.

LSG's 2026 season is over. The questions are just beginning.
author: Diaspora Desk
